record.paper_title: Open Problems in Human Trait Genetics
record.original_question: How should human trait genetics use rare variants—low-frequency variants that may have stronger phenotypic effects but are hard to detect and quantify—to explain missing heritability and improve association studies or polygenic risk scores, given the trade-off between sequencing quality and cohort size and the unresolved question of how to interpret rare variants statistically?

evidence.quote: Whether or not rare variants alone are the main source of missing heritability, by now there is a lot of evidence that they play an important role in many complex traits [71]. Unfortunately, genetic studies still rarely deal with rare variants, and there is shortage of whole-genome and whole-exome sequencing cohorts that can capture them (open problem #4: rare variants).
there is a real trade-off between the quality and quantity of genetic data, and it is not entirely clear which of the two is more critical.
Another problem is that even after a large cohort is fully sequenced, it is not entirely clear how to interpret rare variants.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in human trait genetics; the literature (e.g., Wainschtein et al. 2022 on whole-genome sequencing recovering more heritability, and ongoing UK Biobank / All of Us WGS efforts) provides partial empirical progress but no resolved statistical framework that fully reconciles the quality–quantity trade-off, optimally incorporates rare variants into PRS, or settles the interpretive question. The problem remains open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Recovery of trait heritability from whole genome sequence data
status_evidence.snippet: Whole-genome sequencing analyses recover a larger fraction of heritability than array-based studies, attributing a substantial portion to rare variants.
status_evidence.claim: Partial empirical progress: rare variants captured by WGS account for additional heritability, but methodology and PRS integration remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Rare variant contributions to complex traits — review
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews note ongoing challenges in detection, interpretation, and aggregation of rare variants for complex-trait association.
status_evidence.claim: Statistical interpretation of rare variants remains an open methodological problem.
